name: Negombo
description: The gateway to Sri Lanka, close to the international airport. Home to a Dutch canal, a working fish market, and a calm first or last night on tour.
intro: Negombo is the first or last night of almost every journey, and that is its job: a working fishing town twenty minutes from the international airport, where you can sleep off a flight beside the sea instead of driving into the night. It is also genuinely worth an unhurried morning.

sections.title: A fishing town, not a resort
sections.body: The lagoon has been fished by the same families for generations, and the beach still fills each morning with outrigger canoes coming in on the wind. The Lellama fish market at dawn is the town at full volume — auctioneers, ice, gulls, and the day's catch laid out on the sand.

sections.title: Dutch canal and old churches
sections.body: The Hamilton Canal, cut under Dutch rule to carry cinnamon south to Colombo, runs straight through town and is best seen at first light. Negombo's large Catholic community has left it a skyline of church towers, which is why the coast here is often called Little Rome.

wildlife: Lagoon and mangrove birds — herons, egrets, kingfishers
Wintering waders on the mudflats
Brahminy kites over the fishing beach

facts.label: Best time
facts.value: Year round; December to March is driest

facts.label: Time needed
facts.value: One night, either side of your flight

facts.label: Getting there
facts.value: 20–30 minutes from Bandaranaike International Airport

facts.label: Pairs with
facts.value: An early start north to Wilpattu or Anuradhapura

goodToKnow: The fish market runs from around 6am and is finished by mid-morning.
Sea swimming is best at the northern end of the beach, away from the fishing boats.
A good place to change money and pick up anything forgotten before heading inland.

name: Wilpattu National Park
description: Sri Lanka's largest national park, known for leopard, sloth bear, elephant, its natural lakes (villus), and dry-zone birdlife.
intro: Wilpattu is the largest national park in Sri Lanka and, for our money, the better leopard park — not because there are more leopards than Yala, but because there are fewer jeeps. The park is named for its villus: natural, rain-fed lakes ringed with open grass, where animals come into the open.

sections.title: Villus, and why they matter
sections.body: A villu is a shallow basin that holds rainwater in a landscape that otherwise hides everything in thick dry-zone scrub. Sitting quietly at the edge of one for an hour is a completely different way of watching than driving the tracks, and it is how most of our best sightings happen.

sections.title: How we work the park
sections.body: We go in at opening and stay through the middle of the day when most jeeps have gone back. Tracks, alarm calls from spotted deer and langur, and patience do more here than radio chatter — Nandana reads the park rather than chasing it.

wildlife: Sri Lankan leopard
Sloth bear — best chances June to August, when palu fruit ripens
Asian elephant
Spotted deer, sambar, wild buffalo, mugger crocodile
Dry-zone birds: painted stork, black-necked stork, Sri Lanka junglefowl, changeable hawk-eagle

facts.label: Best time
facts.value: February to October; the park can close in heavy rain

facts.label: Time needed
facts.value: Two nights, for a full day and a half-day drive

facts.label: Getting there
facts.value: About 3 hours from Negombo, 1.5 hours from Anuradhapura

facts.label: Terrain
facts.value: Dry-zone forest, scrub and open villus

goodToKnow: Full-day drives with a packed lunch see far more than a short afternoon circuit.
Sightings are never guaranteed — anyone who promises you a leopard is selling you something.
Bring neutral clothing, a hat and more water than you think you need.

name: Anuradhapura
description: One of Sri Lanka's ancient capitals, with a wide ancient-city complex visited alongside nearby Mihintale Temple.
intro: Anuradhapura was the island's capital for over a thousand years, and it is still a living pilgrimage city rather than a ruin field. White-robed pilgrims, oil lamps and lotus flowers move through monuments that were already ancient when Europe's cathedrals were built.

sections.title: The sacred city
sections.body: At its heart is the Sri Maha Bodhi, a sacred fig grown from a cutting of the tree under which the Buddha attained enlightenment, planted here in the third century BC and tended without a break ever since. Around it stand the great stupas — Ruwanwelisaya, Jetavanaramaya, Abhayagiri — each an enormous solid dome of brick.

sections.title: Mihintale, where it began
sections.body: Twelve kilometres east, a stairway of 1,840 granite steps climbs Mihintale, where the monk Mahinda met King Devanampiya Tissa and Buddhism entered Sri Lanka. Go at first light: the climb is cool, the view over the dry-zone plain is long, and the site is quiet.

wildlife: Grey langur and toque macaque around the ruins
Tank birds — pelicans, painted storks, open-billed storks
Indian peafowl at dawn on the bunds

facts.label: Best time
facts.value: Year round; May to September is hottest

facts.label: Time needed
facts.value: One full day, two if you add Mihintale properly

facts.label: Getting there
facts.value: About 4 hours from Colombo, 1.5 hours from Wilpattu

facts.label: Dress
facts.value: Shoulders and knees covered; shoes off at the sacred sites

goodToKnow: Poya (full moon) days are extraordinary to witness, and very busy.
The site is spread over kilometres — a vehicle between clusters saves the day.
White clothing is the pilgrim's custom, and always welcome.

name: Trincomalee
description: A harbour city on the east coast, the departure point for Pigeon Island and dolphin watching trips.
intro: Trincomalee sits on one of the world's finest natural harbours, on a coast that runs on the opposite season to the rest of the island. When the south-west is under monsoon, Trinco is calm, clear and swimmable.

sections.title: Koneswaram and the harbour
sections.body: The Koneswaram temple stands on Swami Rock above a sheer drop to the sea — a Hindu site of long standing, rebuilt after the Portuguese destroyed the original. Below it the harbour opens out, deep enough to have been fought over by every navy that ever came this way.

sections.title: Reef and open water
sections.body: Pigeon Island, a short boat ride off Nilaveli, is a marine national park with living coral, reef fish and blacktip reef sharks in the shallows. Further out, the deep water off Trincomalee is one of the island's whale grounds in the eastern season.

wildlife: Blue whale and sperm whale offshore, in season
Spinner dolphin, often in large pods
Reef fish, blacktip reef sharks and hawksbill turtles at Pigeon Island
White-bellied sea eagle along the headlands

facts.label: Best time
facts.value: May to September — the east coast's dry season

facts.label: Time needed
facts.value: Two to three nights

facts.label: Getting there
facts.value: About 3 hours from Sigiriya or Polonnaruwa

facts.label: Beaches
facts.value: Uppuveli for quiet, Nilaveli for the Pigeon Island boats

goodToKnow: Snorkelling gear is available locally, but bring your own mask if you are particular.
Reef-safe sunscreen only at Pigeon Island — it is a national park.
Whale watching is weather-dependent and always starts early.

name: Sigiriya
description: Home to the Lion Rock Fortress and Pidurangala Temple, with Polonnaruwa's ancient city and Minneriya National Park nearby.
intro: A granite plug of an extinct volcano rising two hundred metres out of flat forest, with a fifth-century royal citadel on top of it. Sigiriya is the single most photographed thing in Sri Lanka and still worth every step.

sections.title: The climb
sections.body: King Kasyapa built his palace on the summit, reached through a gateway shaped as a lion — only the enormous paws survive. On the way up, a sheltered gallery holds the frescoes of the Sigiriya maidens, painted more than fifteen hundred years ago, and the polished mirror wall carries graffiti left by visitors from the eighth century onward.

sections.title: What most people miss
sections.body: The water gardens at the base are an engineering achievement in their own right, with fountains that still run in the rainy season. And Pidurangala, the rock opposite, is the better sunrise: a rougher scramble, half the crowd, and the view is of Sigiriya itself.

wildlife: Toque macaque and grey langur on the lower terraces
Sri Lanka grey hornbill and Sri Lanka junglefowl in the surrounding forest
Painted-lip lizard on the rock faces
Elephants on the road to Minneriya at dusk

facts.label: Best time
facts.value: Year round; climb at 7am or after 3.30pm

facts.label: Time needed
facts.value: Half a day for the rock, two nights to include Polonnaruwa

facts.label: Getting there
facts.value: About 3.5 hours from Negombo, 1 hour from Polonnaruwa

facts.label: The climb
facts.value: Roughly 1,200 steps, steep metal stairways near the top

goodToKnow: Not one for severe vertigo — the final stairways are open on one side.
Water, hat and an early start; there is no shade on the summit.
Hornets occasionally close sections of the climb; the guards' word is final.

name: Polonnaruwa
description: Sri Lanka's second ancient capital, explored on an ancient-city tour paired with a visit to Minneriya National Park.
intro: The island's second capital, and the most legible ancient city in Sri Lanka: a compact, walkable, cyclable set of palaces, temples and a great reservoir, most of it built in a single burst of twelfth-century confidence.

sections.title: Best seen from a bicycle
sections.body: The ruins are spread across a few flat kilometres of parkland under big trees, which makes a bicycle the right way to see them. The Vatadage, the Lankatilaka image house and the Royal Palace all sit within an easy ride of one another.

sections.title: Gal Vihara
sections.body: Four colossal Buddha figures cut from a single granite face — a seated figure, a small rock cavity image, a standing figure with a rare crossed-arm posture, and a reclining Buddha seven metres longer than a bus. The stone was chosen so the grain runs with the robes, and the carving has not been improved on in eight hundred years.

sections.title: Parakrama Samudra
sections.body: The Sea of Parakrama, an irrigation reservoir large enough to have its own horizon, still waters the paddy around the town. At dusk it is the place to be, and the nearby Minneriya and Kaudulla tanks draw one of Asia's great elephant congregations in the dry months.

wildlife: Asian elephant at Minneriya and Kaudulla, August to September for the Gathering
Tank birds — pelicans, cormorants, egrets, storks
Toque macaque among the ruins
Land monitors and mugger crocodiles on the bunds

facts.label: Best time
facts.value: Year round; the Gathering peaks August to September

facts.label: Time needed
facts.value: One full day, two nights if you add an evening safari

facts.label: Getting there
facts.value: 1 hour from Sigiriya, 3 hours from Kandy

facts.label: Getting around
facts.value: Bicycle, with a vehicle for the outlying groups

goodToKnow: Start at 7am — the site has little shade by eleven.
Shoulders and knees covered; shoes and hats off at the image houses.
The museum by the entrance is worth twenty minutes before you ride out.

name: Kandy
description: The hill-country cultural capital: the Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic, a cultural show, tea factories, and the Dambulla Cave Temple en route.
intro: The last kingdom to fall to the British, held out for three centuries in a bowl of forested hills, and still the ceremonial heart of the island. Kandy is a working city with a lake in the middle and a rainforest reserve on the ridge above it.

sections.title: The Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
sections.body: Sri Dalada Maligawa holds a tooth of the Buddha, and with it a long tradition that whoever holds the relic holds the country. Come for one of the three daily pujas, when the drummers play and the inner chamber is opened; the building itself — dark timber, ivory inlay, painted ceilings — repays a slow walk.

sections.title: Above the city
sections.body: Udawattakele, the old royal forest garden behind the temple, is birding within walking distance of the centre. Three kilometres out, the Royal Botanical Gardens at Peradeniya hold a giant Javan fig, an orchid house and an avenue of palms, with a fruit bat colony overhead that has to be seen at dusk.

wildlife: Layard's parakeet, yellow-fronted barbet and other endemics in Udawattakele
Indian flying fox roosting at Peradeniya
Purple-faced langur in the forest reserve
Water monitors along the lake shore

facts.label: Best time
facts.value: Year round; the Esala Perahera falls in July or August

facts.label: Time needed
facts.value: Two nights

facts.label: Getting there
facts.value: 3 hours from Colombo; the hill-country train leaves from here

facts.label: Altitude
facts.value: About 500 m — cooler and greener than the coast

goodToKnow: The evening puja is the atmospheric one; be there twenty minutes early.
White or modest clothing for the temple, and shoes are left at the entrance.
The Esala Perahera fills the city for ten nights — book far ahead or plan around it.

name: Kithulgala
description: A rainforest-edge village on the Kelani River, known for white-water rafting, canyoning, zip-lining, and rich birdlife.
intro: A rainforest village on the Kelani River, best known for white water and for the bridge that was blown up in The Bridge on the River Kwai. It is also one of the most reliable places on the island for lowland endemic birds, and almost nobody comes here for that.

sections.title: The river
sections.body: The Kelani runs grade two to three through Kithulgala — big enough to be genuinely fun, forgiving enough for a first raft. The same gorge gives canyoning, jumps and natural slides, run by local crews who know exactly which pools are safe at which water level.

sections.title: The forest across the water
sections.body: Makandawa forest reserve is reached by a small ferry across the river and then a climb into wet lowland rainforest. It holds much of the Sinharaja endemic list within a much shorter walk, which makes it a good first rainforest morning before the deeper trip south.

wildlife: Sri Lanka spurfowl, green-billed coucal and chestnut-backed owlet
Sri Lanka blue magpie, layard's parakeet
Mixed-species feeding flocks in the early morning
Hump-nosed lizard and endemic frogs along the streams

facts.label: Best time
facts.value: December to April for rafting; birding is year round

facts.label: Time needed
facts.value: One or two nights

facts.label: Getting there
facts.value: About 2 hours from Colombo, 2.5 hours from Kandy

facts.label: Terrain
facts.value: Wet lowland rainforest, steep and slippery in places

goodToKnow: It rains here — properly — and that is the point of the forest.
Leech socks for the forest walks; the guides carry spares.
Rafting operators vary; we use the same crew every time.

name: Ella
description: A hill-country town reached by one of the world's most scenic train journeys, home to the Nine Arch Bridge, Little Adam's Peak, and Ravana Waterfall.
intro: A gap in the hills where the mountains fall away to the southern plain, wrapped in tea and cloud forest. Ella is small, walkable and has the best short hikes in the hill country coming straight out of the village.

sections.title: Walks from the door
sections.body: Little Adam's Peak is a gentle hour through tea to a ridge with the whole gap laid out below it. Ella Rock is longer, steeper and quieter, and best done early with someone who knows the turning — the path is not signed and half the walkers on it are lost.

sections.title: The bridge and the train
sections.body: The Nine Arches Bridge, built in stone and brick when steel ran short in the First World War, curves through the forest below the village; the train crossing it is one of the sights of the island. The line itself, from Nanu Oya or Haputale down to Ella, is the reason many people come to the hill country at all.

wildlife: Yellow-eared bulbul and Sri Lanka white-eye in the tea and scrub
Crested serpent eagle over the gap
Purple-faced langur in the forest patches
Butterflies in extraordinary numbers after rain

facts.label: Best time
facts.value: January to March; the hills clear in the morning

facts.label: Time needed
facts.value: Two nights

facts.label: Getting there
facts.value: Train from Nanu Oya or Haputale; 3 hours by road from Nuwara Eliya

facts.label: Altitude
facts.value: About 1,040 m — warm days, cool nights

goodToKnow: Book train seats well in advance, or travel in the unreserved carriage and stand at the door.
Cloud closes in by late morning; do the viewpoints early.
Proper shoes for Ella Rock — it is a real hill walk, not a stroll.

name: Yala National Park
description: A dry-zone park of scrub jungle, water reservoirs, brackish lagoons and riverine habitats — the best park in the country to see leopard and sloth bear.
intro: The park that made Sri Lanka a leopard destination: dry scrub, granite outcrops and lagoons meeting the sea, with one of the highest recorded leopard densities anywhere. It is also the busiest park in the country, and how you visit it matters.

sections.title: Leopard country
sections.body: Block 1 is where the density is, and where the jeeps are. We go in at the gate opening, work the quieter western tracks and the rock outcrops where leopards lie up in the morning sun, and avoid the queue that forms around any radio sighting.

sections.title: More than the cats
sections.body: Yala's elephants are here year round; sloth bear appear in the fruiting months; and the coastal lagoons hold flamingo, spoonbill and pelican in the northern winter. The ancient monastery of Sithulpawwa, still in use inside the park boundary, is worth pairing with an afternoon drive.

wildlife: Sri Lankan leopard
Asian elephant and sloth bear
Mugger crocodile, spotted deer, wild buffalo
Migrant waders and flamingo on the lagoons, November to March

facts.label: Best time
facts.value: February to July; the park usually closes in September

facts.label: Time needed
facts.value: Two nights, for a morning and an afternoon drive

facts.label: Getting there
facts.value: About 30 minutes from Tissamaharama

facts.label: Alternative
facts.value: Bundala, nearby, for wetland birds and no crowds

goodToKnow: First jeep through the gate sees a different park to the tenth.
Stay in the vehicle and keep the noise down — this is the whole etiquette.
Block 1 is busy; ask us about Block 5 and Bundala for quieter mornings.

name: Sinharaja Rain Forest
description: A UNESCO World Heritage Site holding the richest biodiversity in Asia, and home to most of Sri Lanka's endemic flora and fauna.
intro: The last substantial stand of primary lowland rainforest in Sri Lanka, a UNESCO World Heritage site, and the single best place in the country to see endemic birds. It rains, it drips, there are leeches, and it is unmissable.

sections.title: Walking in the forest
sections.body: There is no driving here: you walk, slowly, on forest tracks with a permit and a guide. Sinharaja's birds move in mixed-species feeding flocks — twenty or thirty birds of a dozen species travelling together — and half the skill is standing still in the right place when one arrives.

sections.title: Endemics
sections.body: Of Sri Lanka's endemic birds, the great majority can be found in this forest, several of them almost nowhere else. Nandana has been walking these trails since his conservation days, and knows the flock routes, the roosts and the calls.

wildlife: Sri Lanka blue magpie, red-faced malkoha, green-billed coucal
Sri Lanka spurfowl and Sri Lanka scaly thrush
Purple-faced langur, giant squirrel
Endemic frogs, agamid lizards and rainforest butterflies

facts.label: Best time
facts.value: January to April and August to September, between monsoons

facts.label: Time needed
facts.value: Two nights, for two full mornings in the forest

facts.label: Getting there
facts.value: Kudawa entrance, about 4 hours from Colombo

facts.label: Terrain
facts.value: Wet, steep, slippery — a real forest, not a park

goodToKnow: Leech socks, rain cover for the camera, and no umbrella in the flock.
Mornings are for birding; afternoons are usually rain.
Groups are kept small and permits are issued at the gate — we handle that.

name: Nuwara Eliya
description: A cool-climate hill station, home to Victoria Park and the gateway to Horton Plains National Park.
intro: Tea country at nineteen hundred metres, laid out by homesick British planters and still full of hedges, racecourses and gabled roofs. It is the coldest town in Sri Lanka and the greenest, and its small municipal park is one of the finest birding sites in the country.

sections.title: Tea, properly explained
sections.body: The hills around town are covered in it, and a factory visit here is worth doing once: the plucking, the withering lofts, the rolling and the grading, followed by a tasting that will spoil supermarket tea for you permanently.

sections.title: Victoria Park
sections.body: A public garden in the middle of town that happens to be a magnet for rare wintering birds. Kashmir flycatcher, pied thrush and Indian pitta are all regular here between November and March, in a park with a bandstand and a children's playground.

wildlife: Kashmir flycatcher, pied thrush and Indian pitta in winter
Sri Lanka bush warbler and yellow-eared bulbul
Sambar deer, which walk into town after dark
Hill-country endemics on the Pedro Estate tracks

facts.label: Best time
facts.value: January to March for birds; April for the season

facts.label: Time needed
facts.value: One or two nights

facts.label: Getting there
facts.value: 2.5 hours from Kandy; the train stops at Nanu Oya

facts.label: Altitude
facts.value: 1,868 m — bring something warm for the evening

goodToKnow: Nights are genuinely cold and most hotels have no heating.
April is Sri Lanka's holiday season here; the town fills and prices rise.
Victoria Park charges a small entry fee and opens early — go at first light.

name: Horton Plains National Park
description: Montane grassland and cloud forest at altitude, home to several of Sri Lanka's highland endemic birds.
intro: A high plateau of montane grassland and cloud forest above two thousand metres, where the island simply stops: at World's End the ground falls away eight hundred and eighty metres in one step, with the southern plains laid out below.

sections.title: The loop walk
sections.body: A circuit of about nine kilometres takes in Little World's End, World's End itself and Baker's Falls, over grassland, through cloud forest and across streams. It is not difficult, but the altitude and the early start are real; most people are back at the car park by mid-morning.

sections.title: Why you start at dawn
sections.body: The escarpment clouds over almost every day between nine and ten, and once it does, World's End is a white wall. Being at the gate when it opens is the whole trick — it also gives you the plateau at its best, frosted in places, with sambar grazing in the open.

wildlife: Sri Lanka whistling thrush at first light near the streams
Sri Lanka bush warbler, dull-blue flycatcher, yellow-eared bulbul
Sambar deer in the grassland
Purple-faced langur (the montane bear monkey) in the cloud forest

facts.label: Best time
facts.value: January to March, driest and clearest

facts.label: Time needed
facts.value: A half day, from a base at Nuwara Eliya or Ella

facts.label: Getting there
facts.value: About 1.5 hours by road from Nuwara Eliya

facts.label: The walk
facts.value: 9.5 km loop, 3 to 4 hours, at 2,100–2,300 m

goodToKnow: Leave at 5.30am — the view closes with the cloud by mid-morning.
It is near freezing at dawn and warm by nine; dress in layers.
No plastic is allowed past the gate and the rangers check bags.

name: Tissamaharama
description: A base town near Yala, with birding around its ancient water tanks and a nearby bird sanctuary.
intro: A quiet town built around an ancient reservoir and a white stupa, and the natural base for Yala and Bundala. Most people sleep here and see nothing of it, which is a pity — the tank at dawn is as good as anything inside the parks.

sections.title: The tank and the stupa
sections.body: Tissa Wewa was built more than two thousand years ago and still irrigates the paddy around town. Its bund at first light, with the Tissamaharama stupa behind it and pelicans working the shallows, is one of the calmest half-hours in the south.

sections.title: Bundala, the birder's park
sections.body: Half an hour away, Bundala is a Ramsar wetland of lagoons and dunes where greater flamingo winter in numbers, along with thousands of migrant waders. There are elephants and crocodiles too, and a fraction of Yala's traffic.

sections.title: Kataragama
sections.body: Twenty kilometres north, Kataragama is one of the island's most important pilgrimage towns, sacred to Buddhists, Hindus and Muslims alike. The evening puja, with drums and fire, is an extraordinary thing to stand at the edge of.

wildlife: Greater flamingo at Bundala, November to March
Painted stork, spoonbill and thousands of migrant waders
Asian elephant on the Bundala tracks
Mugger crocodile in the tanks

facts.label: Best time
facts.value: November to March for the migrants; February to July for Yala

facts.label: Time needed
facts.value: Two nights, as the base for the southern parks

facts.label: Getting there
facts.value: About 5 hours from Ella, 4 hours from Mirissa

facts.label: Nearby
facts.value: Yala 30 minutes, Bundala 30 minutes, Kataragama 30 minutes

goodToKnow: Safari jeeps leave around 5am — dinner early the night before.
The tank bund is a public road; walk it at dawn with binoculars.
Kataragama is a place of worship first and a sight second; dress and behave accordingly.

name: Mirissa
description: A south-coast beach town, paired with a visit to Galle's Dutch Fort.
intro: The end of the journey for most of our itineraries: a curve of sand on the south coast with palms leaning over it, warm water, and the deepest whale-watching ground in Sri Lanka just offshore.

sections.title: Blue whales
sections.body: The continental shelf comes close to the coast here, which puts blue whales — the largest animal that has ever lived — within a couple of hours of the harbour. Sperm whales, Bryde's whales and big pods of spinner dolphins use the same water. Boats leave before dawn.

sections.title: The coast either side
sections.body: Weligama, next door, is where everyone learns to surf, on a long forgiving beach break. Galle, an hour west, is a Dutch fort town of ramparts, warehouses and shuttered houses that is worth a full afternoon and an evening walk on the walls.

wildlife: Blue whale and sperm whale, November to April
Spinner dolphin, often in hundreds
Green turtles in the shallows at Hikkaduwa and Habaraduwa
Sea eagles and terns along the headlands

facts.label: Best time
facts.value: November to April — the south coast's dry season

facts.label: Time needed
facts.value: Two or three nights to finish a journey

facts.label: Getting there
facts.value: About 2.5 hours from Tissamaharama; 2 hours from Colombo by expressway

facts.label: Nearby
facts.value: Weligama for surf, Galle Fort for an afternoon

goodToKnow: Whale boats leave at 6am and the sea is calmest early.
Choose an operator that keeps the legal distance — we book responsibly or not at all.
The bay has a strong current at the eastern end; swim towards the middle.
